arxiv-1907-02971.title: Higher-Order Sudakov Resummation in Coupled Gauge Theories
arxiv-1907-02971.creator: and Jim Talbert
arxiv-1907-02971.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by and Jim Talbert. We consider the higher-order resummation of Sudakov double logarithms in the presence of multiple coupled gauge interactions. The associated evolution equations depend on the coupled β \beta functions of two (or more) coupling constants α a \alpha_{a} and α b \alpha_{b} , as well as anomalous dimensions that have joint perturbative series in α a \alpha_{a} and α b \alpha_{b} . We discuss possible strategies for solving the system of evolution equations that arises.

arxiv-1912-03048.title: Document Network Embedding: Coping for Missing Content and Missing Links Conference: ; ; CCS: Computing methodologies Machine translation CCS: Computing methodologies Learning latent representations CCS: Information systems Information retrieval
arxiv-1912-03048.creator: Jean Dupuy, Adrien Guille, Julien Jacques
arxiv-1912-03048.description: Abstract . Searching through networks of documents is an important task. A promising path to improve the performance of information retrieval systems in this context is to leverage dense node and content representations learned with embedding techniques. However, these techniques cannot learn representations for documents that are either isolated or whose content is missing.

arxiv-2105-05296.title: Online POMDP Planning via Simplification
arxiv-2105-05296.creator: Ori Sztyglic, Vadim Indelman
arxiv-2105-05296.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider online planning in partially observable domains. Solving the corresponding POMDP problem is a very challenging task, particularly in an online setting. Our key contribution is a novel algorithmic approach, Simplified Information Theoretic Belief Space Planning (SITH-BSP), which aims to speed-up POMDP planning considering belief-dependent rewards, without compromising on the solution’s accuracy.

arxiv-2207-05738.title: PAC Reinforcement Learning for Predictive State Representations
arxiv-2207-05738.creator: Wenhao Zhan, Masatoshi Uehara, Wen Sun, Jason D. Lee
arxiv-2207-05738.description: Abstract In this paper we study online Reinforcement Learning (RL) in partially observable dynamical systems. We focus on the Predictive State Representations (PSRs) model, which is an expressive model that captures other well-known models such as Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDP).

arxiv-2308-04076.title: \datatales : Investigating the use of Large Language Models for Authoring Data-Driven Articles
arxiv-2308-04076.creator: Nicole Sultanum, Arjun Srinivasan
arxiv-2308-04076.description: Abstract Authoring data-driven articles is a complex process requiring authors to not only analyze data for insights but also craft a cohesive narrative that effectively communicates the insights. Text generation capabilities of contemporary large language models (LLMs) present an opportunity to assist the authoring of data-driven articles and expedite the writing process.

arxiv-2405-14541.title: Concurrence of directional Kondo transport and incommensurate magnetic order in the layered material AgCrSe 2 \text{AgCrSe}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}
arxiv-2405-14541.creator: José Guimarães, Dorsa S. Fartab, Michal Moravec, Marcus Schmidt, Michael Baenitz, Burkhard Schmidt, Haijing Zhang
arxiv-2405-14541.description: Abstract I Abstract In this work, we report on the concurrent emergence of the directional Kondo behavior and incommensurate magnetic ordering in a layered material. We employ temperature- and magnetic field-dependent resistivity measurements, susceptibility measurements, and high resolution wavelength X-ray diffraction spectroscopy to study the electronic properties of AgCrSe 2 \text{AgCrSe}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} .

arxiv-2409-04492.title: Nonlinear Fenchel Conjugates
arxiv-2409-04492.creator: Anton Schiela, Roland Herzog, Ronny Bergmann
arxiv-2409-04492.description: Abstract . The classical concept of Fenchel conjugation is tailored to extended real-valued functions defined on linear spaces. In this paper we generalize this concept to functions defined on arbitrary sets that do not necessarily bear any structure at all. This generalization is obtained by replacing linear test functions by general nonlinear ones.

arxiv-2411-12610.title: Universal programmable waveguide arrays
arxiv-2411-12610.creator: Akram Youssry, Alberto Peruzzo
arxiv-2411-12610.description: Abstract Implementing arbitrary unitary transformations is crucial for applications in quantum computing, signal processing, and machine learning. Unitaries govern quantum state evolution, enabling reversible transformations critical in quantum tasks like cryptography and simulation and playing key roles in classical domains such as dimensionality reduction and signal compression.

arxiv-2508-18798.title: CASP: An evaluation dataset for formal verification of C code
arxiv-2508-18798.creator: Niclas Hertzberg, Merlijn Sevenhuijsen, Liv Kåreborn, Anna Lokrantz
arxiv-2508-18798.description: Abstract Recent developments in Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating code generation, yet the generated programs lack rigorous correctness guarantees. Formal verification can address this shortcoming, but requires expertise and is time-consuming to apply. Currently, there is no dataset of verified C code paired with formal specifications that enables systematic benchmarking in this space.

britannica-1911-walthamstow.title: Walthamstow (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-walthamstow.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-walthamstow.description: Article 'Walthamstow' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. parliamentary division of Essex, England, a short distance E. of the river Lea, with several stations on a branch of the Great Eastern railway, 6 m. of Liverpool Street station. of urban district (1891) 46,346; (1901) 95,131. It is sheltered on the north and east by low hills formerly included in Epping Forest.

plos-pone-0006701.creator: Yunqi Li, Ambrish Roy, Yang Zhang
plos-pone-0006701.description: PLOS ONE research article. Hydrogen constitutes nearly half of all atoms in proteins and their positions are essential for analyzing hydrogen-bonding interactions and refining atomic-level structures. However, most protein structures determined by experiments or computer prediction lack hydrogen coordinate

pmc-11346965.title: Influence of surprise on reinforcement learning in younger and older adults
pmc-11346965.creator: Christoph Koch, Ondrej Zika, Rasmus Bruckner, Nicolas W. Schuck, Thomas Serre, Tobias U Hauser, Thomas Serre, Tobias U Hauser, Thomas Serre, Tobias U Hauser
pmc-11346965.description: Surprise is a key component of many learning experiences, and yet its precise computational role, and how it changes with age, remain debated. One major challenge is that surprise often occurs jointly with other variables, such as uncertainty and outcome probability.

pmc-11548385.title: Characterization of Mixtures Based on High-Density Polyethylene and Plasticized Starch
pmc-11548385.creator: Maria Daniela Stelescu, Ovidiu-Cristian Oprea, Doina Constantinescu, Ludmila Motelica, Anton Ficai, Roxana-Doina Trusca, Maria Sonmez, Dana Florentina Gurau, Mihai Georgescu, Rodica Roxana Constantinescu, Bogdan-Stefan Vasile, Denisa Ficai, Rongfeng Li, Guantian Li, Kun Gao
pmc-11548385.description: This paper presents the obtaining and characterization of blends based on high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and plasticized starch. In addition to plasticized starch (28.8% w/w), the compositions made also contained other ingredients, such as polyethylene-graft-maleic anhydride as a compatibilizer, ethylene propylene terpolymer elastomer, cross-linking agents, and nanoclay. Plasticized starch contains 68.6% w/w potato starch, 29.

pmc-11578427.title: Lobatozoum woodi n. sp. (Digenea: Didymozoidae) parasitizing Euthynnus alletteratus (Scombriformes: Scombridae) in the coast of the State of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
pmc-11578427.creator: Robertta Gitahy Freire, Marcia Cristina Nascimento Justo, Yuri Costa Meneses, Alena Mayo Iñiguez, Simone Chinicz Cohen
pmc-11578427.description: The aim of this study was to describe a new species of Didymozoidae (Trematoda) found in the mesentery of Euthynnus alletteratus (Rafinesque) off Cabo Frio, in the coastal area of the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Thirty specimens of E. alletteratus were obtained between August 2023 and June 2024, directly from traders who sell fresh fish in markets.

pmc-11635906.title: The Combination of a Donor–Acceptor TADF and a MR‐TADF Emitting Core Results in Outstanding Electroluminescence Performance
pmc-11635906.creator: Dongyang Chen, Hui Wang, Dianming Sun, Sen Wu, Kai Wang, Xiao‐Hong Zhang, Eli Zysman‐Colman
pmc-11635906.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Here the utility and potential of an emitter design are demonstrated, consisting of a narrowband‐emitting multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR‐TADF) core that is decorated with a suitably higher energy donor‐acceptor TADF moiety. Not only does this D–A TADF group offer additional channels for triplet exciton harvesting and confers faster reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) kinetics but it also acts as a steric shield, insulating the emissive MR‐TADF core from aggregation‐caused quenching.

pmc-12118673.title: Super-resolution imaging of the neuronal cytoskeleton
pmc-12118673.creator: Ciarán Butler-Hallissey, Christophe Leterrier
pmc-12118673.description: The complexity of the brain organization and the unique architecture of neurons have motivated neuroscientists to stay at the forefront of cellular microscopy and rapidly take advantage of technical developments in this field. Among these developments, super-resolution microscopy has transformed our understanding of neurobiology by allowing us to image identified macromolecular scaffolds and complexes directly in cells.

pmc-12438302.title: “Step by Step” Toward Recovery for People with Severe Mental Illness – The Example of a Community Mental Health Structure on the Outskirts of Lisbon
pmc-12438302.creator: M Andrade, F Ramalheira, A Nunes, L Gil
pmc-12438302.description: IntroductionAddressing severe mental illness requires assertive community intervention. The “Assertive Program – Step by Step”, implemented in 2016, involves a mental health team in the Sintra region (Lisbon). Through a case manager model and regular patient contact, an Individualized Care Plan is developed to ensure treatment continuity, coordinate psychosocial interventions, and reduce both the frequency and duration of hospital admissions.

pmc-12519656.title: Do variants in the CDH23 gene cause non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa? Dual validation using whole exome sequencing and a zebrafish model
pmc-12519656.creator: Xue Fan, Shiqin Yuan, Jingxia Wen, Shaolin Wang, Weining Rong, Dongling Feng
pmc-12519656.description: ObjectiveUsing whole exome sequencing to detect pathogenic genes in families with inherited retinal dystrophy, and also to investigate the effects of CDH23 gene knockdown on the retinal structure of zebrafish.MethodsIn this study, we collected data from a patient diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) at Ningxia Eye Hospital in 2022.

pmc-12645753.title: When injury costs too much: the catastrophic costs for spinal cord injury in Iran
pmc-12645753.creator: Shahrokh Yousefzadeh-Chabok, Diana Pacheco Barzallo, Zahra Mohtasham-Amiri, Enayatollah Homaie Rad
pmc-12645753.description: IntroductionThe main objective of this study was to determine the percentage of families experiencing catastrophic costs as a result of spinal cord injury. Patients with spinal cord injuries often encounter significant expenses related to treatment, rehabilitation, and caregiving. Catastrophic expenditures are the direct consequence of the lack of effective health insurance.

pmc-13038714.title: Machine learning-based model for prediction of KCNJ5 mutation in unilateral primary aldosteronism based on [68Ga]Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT
pmc-13038714.creator: Rui Zuo, Zhaoming Chen, Zhengjie Wang, Shenglong Li, Wenbo Li, Zhu Xia, Hua Pang, Lu Xu
pmc-13038714.description: BackgroundKCNJ5 mutations enhance aldosterone synthase expression and are closely associated with the prognosis of unilateral primary aldosteronism (UPA). This study developed machine learning-based models with [68Ga]Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT for predicting KCNJ5 mutations in patients with UPA.ResultsMost of the clinical characteristics and all of [68Ga]Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT parameters differed significantly between the KCNJ5-MT and KCNJ5-WT patients.

pmc-13116623.title: Population-Specific Mutational Spectrum of Autosomal Recessive Nonsyndromic Hearing Loss in Croatian Roma: Implications for Clinical Genetics
pmc-13116623.creator: Iva Kutija Fučkar, Matea Zajc Petranović, Irena Martinović Klarić, Marijana Peričić Salihović, Lovorka Barać Lauc
pmc-13116623.description: Background/Objectives: Hearing impairment is a highly prevalent sensory disorder resulting from a variety of causes. A high proportion of autosomal recessive non-syndromic hearing impairment is linked to the GJB2 (OMIM 121011) gene which encodes for a gap junction protein, connexin-26. Alterations of genes that encode for connexins can lead to changes in cell ion content and cause hearing impairment.

pmc-13571691.title: Application of Human Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Derived Exosomes in Gastrointestinal Diseases
pmc-13571691.creator: Zhiliang Mai, Ningning Yue, Hailan Zhao, Lisheng Wang, Defeng Li
pmc-13571691.description: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases are increasing in prevalence worldwide and represent a major public health burden. However, current treatments remain limited and are often associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) have emerged as promising candidates because of their anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and regenerative properties.

uslaw-usc-t16-s757c.title: 16 U.S.C. § 757c — Approval for activities on land administered by other Federal departments or agencies
uslaw-usc-t16-s757c.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s757c.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 9A (Preservation Of Fishery Resources). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Activities authorized by sections 757a to 757f of this title to be performed on lands administered by other Federal departments or agencies shall be carried out only with the prior approval of such departments or agencies.
